clean.tl: I always open my letters myself.' (-)

clean.tx: izaho ihany no naka ny sary

clean.tl: The father himself dies.' (FOC: focus particle; mihitsy is used if the head NP is a full noun phrase; with pronouns, tena is regularly used)
The house itself collapsed.' (FOC: focus particle; mihitsy is possible with inanimate head NPs)

Koto can see himself.' (NA: nominal article; determiner which is used only with proper names; tena incorporated into the verb (cf. Zribi-Hertz & Rajaonarisoa 1999); sometimes with middle semantics; this is probably responsible for the modal component (can see himself))

Koto sees his self. (his body).' (NA: nominal article; determiner which is used only with proper names tena as lexical N-head within a DP (possessive tena) possessive tena is not syntactically incorporated into the verb (cf. Zribi-Hertz 1999) it indicates semantic reflexivity as opposed to incorporated tena, which tends to show middle semantics)
Paul intended to save himself.' (NA: nominal article; determiner which is used only with proper names)
He himself arrived. (lit.: arrived he his-body)' (tena-ny is used in association with pronominals; if the preceding nominal is an NP mihitsy (indeed) is used)
I will go to your farm.
